questions.question: Tapan Kumar Pattanayak won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhau** is a traditional Indian dance form with origins in the eastern states of India, particularly West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Odisha.
 
• It is known for its vigorous movements and martial arts-inspired choreography, often depicting stories from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• Chhau dance is performed during local festivals and is a blend of folk and classical elements, using elaborate masks and costumes.
 
• In 2010, UNESCO inscribed Chhau dance in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**

 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.
 
• It is conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance and Drama.
 
• The award is given to artists who have made a significant contribution to their respective fields and has categories for music, dance, theatre, and other traditional arts.
 
• Recipients of the award receive a citation, a plaque, and a cash prize.
 
 
 
• **Other Dance Forms Mentioned**
 
 
• **Sattriya**: A classical dance-drama performance art of Assam, Sattriya was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnava saint Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev.
 
• **Odissi**: Originating from the state of Odisha, Odissi is one of the oldest surviving dance forms in India, known for its graceful movements and sculpturesque poses.
 
• **Kuchipudi**: This classical dance form hails from Andhra Pradesh and combines dance, music, and acting, often telling stories from Hindu epics.

questions.question: Which regulatory body in India oversees and supervises microfinance institutions (MFIs) to ensure their compliance with regulations?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of India, which regulates the banking and financial sectors in the country.
 
• RBI has the authority to regulate and supervise microfinance institutions (MFIs) to ensure their compliance with the regulatory framework.
 
• The regulations set by the RBI help in maintaining the financial stability and transparency of MFIs.
 
• RBI's regulations are aimed at protecting the interests of borrowers and maintaining the integrity of the microfinance sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance Institutions (MFIs)**

 
 
• MFIs are financial institutions that provide small loans and other financial services to low-income individuals or groups who lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• These institutions play a crucial role in promoting financial inclusion by providing credit to economically weaker sections of society.
 
• MFIs typically offer loans for income-generating activities, thereby helping borrowers to improve their livelihoods and escape poverty.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**
 
 
• The RBI, established in 1935, is the central bank of India and is responsible for regulating the monetary and financial system of the country.
 
• It regulates the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee and manages the country's main payment systems.
 
• The RBI is also responsible for overseeing the country's foreign exchange and gold reserves.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework for MFIs**
 
 
• The RBI sets guidelines and regulations for MFIs to ensure they operate in a transparent and accountable manner.
 
• These regulations include guidelines on interest rates, loan disbursement processes, and borrower protection measures.
 
• The objective is to protect borrowers from excessive interest rates and ensure fair lending practices.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**
 
 
• Financial inclusion is the process of ensuring access to financial services and timely and adequate credit where needed by vulnerable groups such as weaker sections and low-income groups at an affordable cost.
 
• It aims to eliminate barriers that exclude people from participating in the financial sector and enable them to access financial products and services.
 
• Financial inclusion is seen as a key driver for socio-economic development and poverty alleviation.

questions.question: Implementation of family planning Programmes were amongst major targets of which of the following five year plan of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth five year plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fourth Five Year Plan of India was implemented from 1969 to 1974.
 
• One of the major targets during this plan was the implementation of family planning programs to control the population growth.
 
• The plan aimed to improve the agricultural sector and achieve self-sufficiency in food grains.
 
• It also focused on industrial development and the promotion of social welfare schemes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Family Planning Programmes**

 
 
• The family planning programmes aimed at controlling the population growth by promoting the use of contraceptives and educating the population about the benefits of smaller family sizes.
 
• These programmes were essential to ensure sustainable development and reduce the strain on resources.
 
• The government also introduced incentives for families who adopted family planning measures.
 
 
 
• **Self-Sufficiency in Food Grains**
 
 
• The Fourth Five Year Plan emphasized achieving self-sufficiency in food grains to reduce dependence on imports.
 
• Efforts were made to increase agricultural productivity through the adoption of modern farming techniques and the use of high-yielding variety seeds.
 
• Support was also provided to farmers in terms of subsidies and access to credit.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Development**
 
 
• The plan focused on promoting industrial growth to create employment opportunities and boost the economy.
 
• It encouraged the establishment of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and provided support for the modernization of existing industries.
 
 
 
• **Social Welfare Schemes**
 
 
• Various social welfare schemes were introduced to improve the living standards of the population.
 
• These included initiatives for education, healthcare, and housing.
 
• The plan also aimed at reducing poverty and promoting social equity.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of Indian Constitution under the fundamental duties is related to the value and preservation of the rich heritage of our composite culture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A(f)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 51A(f)** of the Indian Constitution states that it is the duty of every citizen of India to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• This article is part of the **Fundamental Duties** which were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations on the citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• There are a total of 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• They are inspired by the Constitution of erstwhile USSR (now Russia).
 
• Originally, the Constitution of India did not contain these duties.
 
• There were originally ten duties, but the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added an eleventh duty.
 
• The duties apply only to citizens and not to foreigners.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• Also known as the Mini-Constitution, it was enacted during the Emergency by the Indira Gandhi government.
 
• This amendment brought about comprehensive changes to the Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
• It also introduced changes in the Preamble and gave more powers to the central government vis-à-vis state governments.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee**
 
 
• This committee was set up in 1976 to make recommendations about fundamental duties.
 
• It was chaired by Sardar Swaran Singh, who was then the Minister of External Affairs.
 
• The committee recommended the inclusion of a separate chapter on Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution is mentioned under the Right to Equality?

options.text: Protection of life and personal liberty

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abolition of titles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Right to Equality** is one of the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution of India.
 
• Article 18 of the Indian Constitution deals with the **Abolition of titles** and is a part of the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18).
 
• Article 18 prohibits the state from conferring any title on any citizen or non-citizen, except military and academic distinctions.
 
• This article aims to prevent the creation of a hierarchical society and ensure that all citizens are treated equally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14**

 
 
• Article 14 guarantees **equality before the law** and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• This article is the cornerstone of the Right to Equality and ensures that no person is discriminated against on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
 
 
• **Article 15**
 
 
• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth**.
 
• It allows the state to make special provisions for women and children, and for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens or for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **Article 16**
 
 
• Article 16 guarantees **equality of opportunity in matters of public employment**.
 
• This article ensures that no citizen shall be discriminated against on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence, or any of them in respect of any employment or office under the State.
 
 
 
• **Article 17**
 
 
• Article 17 abolishes **untouchability** and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• The enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability shall be an offense punishable in accordance with law.

questions.question: Which of the following is required by the aquatic animals to breathe under water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dissolved Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Most aquatic animals, including fish, require **dissolved oxygen** in water to breathe.
 
• Dissolved oxygen is oxygen that is **mixed into water** and is essential for the survival of aquatic organisms.
 
• Aquatic animals extract dissolved oxygen from water through their gills or other respiratory surfaces.
 
• Low levels of dissolved oxygen in water can lead to **hypoxia**, which can be detrimental to aquatic life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dissolved Oxygen (DO)**

 
 
• It refers to the amount of oxygen that is present in water. The level of dissolved oxygen is an important indicator of water quality.
 
• DO is essential for the respiration of aquatic life, especially fish, invertebrates, and aerobic bacteria.
 
• Factors that affect DO levels include water temperature, salinity, and the presence of organic matter.
 
• DO levels can be measured using various methods such as chemical titration, electrochemical analysis, and optical sensors.
 
 
 
• **Hypoxia**
 
 
• It is a condition in which there is a deficiency of oxygen in the water, leading to an environment where aquatic life struggles to survive.
 
• Hypoxia can be caused by various factors, including pollution, excessive nutrient runoff, and algal blooms.
 
• Prolonged hypoxic conditions can result in "dead zones" where most marine life cannot survive.
 
 
 
• **Gills**
 
 
• Gills are the respiratory organs of fish and some other aquatic animals.
 
• They allow these animals to extract dissolved oxygen from water and expel carbon dioxide.
 
• Gills are highly efficient at oxygen exchange, and their large surface area facilitates the diffusion of gases.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen Solubility**
 
 
• The solubility of oxygen in water decreases as the temperature increases.
 
• Cold water can hold more dissolved oxygen compared to warm water.
 
• Salinity also affects oxygen solubility; freshwater can hold more dissolved oxygen than saltwater.

questions.question: Which country is India's neighbour to the west, sharing a significant border, and is often a topic of geopolitical significance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Geographical Location:** Pakistan is located to the west of India and shares a significant border with it.
 
• **Historical Context:** The India-Pakistan border was established following the partition of British India in 1947, which led to the creation of Pakistan.
 
• **Geopolitical Significance:** The relationship between India and Pakistan is of major geopolitical importance due to historical conflicts and ongoing territorial disputes, particularly over the region of Kashmir.
 
• **Border Length:** The India-Pakistan border is approximately 3,323 kilometers long and is one of the most heavily militarized borders in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Partition of British India:**

 
 
• The partition of British India in 1947 resulted in the creation of two independent dominions: India and Pakistan.
 
• The partition led to one of the largest mass migrations in human history and significant communal violence.
 
• The Radcliffe Line, named after its architect Sir Cyril Radcliffe, was the boundary demarcation line between India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pakistani Wars:**
 
 
• India and Pakistan have fought three major wars since their independence: in 1947, 1965, and 1971.
 
• The 1971 war led to the creation of Bangladesh, formerly East Pakistan.
 
• There have also been numerous skirmishes and border conflicts, particularly in the Kashmir region.
 
 
 
• **Kashmir Conflict:**
 
 
• The Kashmir conflict is a territorial dispute between India and Pakistan over the Kashmir region.
 
• Both countries claim the region in full but control only parts of it.
 
• The conflict has resulted in several wars and ongoing military standoffs.
 
 
 
• **Line of Control (LoC):**
 
 
• The Line of Control (LoC) is the de facto border between India and Pakistan in the region of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It was established following the Simla Agreement in 1972 after the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971.
 
• The LoC is highly militarized and often a site of conflict and skirmishes between the two countries.

questions.question: Which of the following festival has 'Jalli Kattu' as a feature ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pongal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pongal** is a major harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu, a state in southern India.
 
• **Jalli Kattu** is a traditional event involving bulls, which is held as part of the Pongal festivities.
 
• This festival typically takes place in mid-January and lasts for four days, each day having its own significance.
 
• Pongal is named after the traditional dish prepared during the festival, which is made of newly harvested rice, milk, and jaggery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jalli Kattu**

 
 
• Jalli Kattu, also known as "Eru Thazhuvuthal" and "Mancuvirattu," is a traditional bull-taming sport played in Tamil Nadu as part of the Pongal celebrations.
 
• The sport is usually held on the third day of Pongal, known as "Mattu Pongal," which is dedicated to cattle.
 
• Participants attempt to grab the hump of the bulls and hold on to them for a certain distance or time.
 
• Jalli Kattu has been a subject of controversy due to concerns about animal welfare, but it remains an integral part of Tamil culture and tradition.
 
 
 
• **Pongal Festival Days**
 
 
• **Bhogi Pongal:** The first day of Pongal is dedicated to Lord Indra, the god of rain, to seek his blessings for the agricultural prosperity of the land.
 
• **Surya Pongal:** The second day is dedicated to the Sun God, Surya, and is the main day of the Pongal festival. The traditional dish "Pongal" is prepared and offered to the Sun God.
 
• **Mattu Pongal:** The third day is dedicated to cattle, which play a crucial role in agriculture. Cows and bulls are decorated, and events like Jalli Kattu are held.
 
• **Kaanum Pongal:** The fourth day is a time for socializing and family reunions, where people visit friends and relatives and exchange gifts.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Pongal Dish**
 
 
• The Pongal dish is a sweet rice pudding made from freshly harvested rice, milk, and jaggery (a type of unrefined sugar).
 
• It is cooked in clay pots, which are decorated with patterns and flowers.
 
• The dish symbolizes abundance and prosperity and is offered to the Sun God as a thanksgiving for the harvest.
 
• The word "Pongal" in Tamil means "to boil over," signifying the overflowing of rice and milk during preparation, which is considered auspicious.

questions.question: According to the data from the Ministry of Mines, the largest resources of gold ore (primary) are located in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihar has the largest resources of gold ore (primary) in India as per the Ministry of Mines data.
 
• The state is known for its diverse mineral resources, including gold.
 
• Bihar's rich mineral wealth includes significant deposits of gold ore, which are crucial for the mining industry.
 
• The presence of these resources can potentially contribute to the state's economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gold Ore**

 
 
• Gold ore is a type of rock that contains significant amounts of gold, which can be extracted through mining.
 
• Gold ores are categorized based on their mineralogy and geology, with primary gold ores being those found in hard rock formations.
 
• The extraction of gold from ore typically involves processes like crushing, milling, and chemical treatment to release the gold particles.
 
• Gold is highly valued for its rarity and diverse applications, including in jewelry, electronics, and as a financial asset.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Mines**
 
 
• The Ministry of Mines is an Indian government ministry responsible for the survey and exploration of all minerals (excluding natural gas and petroleum).
 
• The ministry oversees the management of mineral resources and the regulation of the mining sector in India.
 
• It also coordinates with state governments to ensure the sustainable development and utilization of mineral resources.
 
• The ministry's initiatives aim to enhance the contribution of the mining sector to the Indian economy.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of Mining**
 
 
• Mining plays a crucial role in the economic development of a region by providing employment opportunities and contributing to infrastructure development.
 
• The extraction and processing of minerals can lead to the establishment of related industries and services, boosting local economies.
 
• Revenue generated from mining activities can be used for public welfare and development projects.
 
• However, mining activities must be managed sustainably to minimize environmental impact and ensure long-term benefits.
 
 
 
• **Bihar's Mineral Resources**
 
 
• Bihar is endowed with a variety of mineral resources, including gold, limestone, mica, and bauxite.
 
• The state's mineral wealth presents opportunities for mining and industrial development.
 
• Efforts are being made to explore and exploit these resources in an environmentally responsible manner.
 
• Development of the mining sector can significantly contribute to Bihar's economic growth and employment generation.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Shunga Dynasty in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pushyamitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pushyamitra Shunga was the founder and first ruler of the Shunga Dynasty in India.
 
• He established the Shunga Dynasty around 185 BCE after assassinating the last Mauryan king, Brihadratha.
 
• Pushyamitra was originally a general in the Mauryan army before he declared himself king.
 
• His reign is marked by the revival of Brahmanism and the decline of Buddhism in some regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shunga Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Shunga Dynasty was an ancient Indian dynasty that followed the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• It was established by Pushyamitra Shunga after the fall of the Maurya Empire.
 
• The Shunga Dynasty is known for its patronage of Brahmanism and Hinduism.
 
• The dynasty ruled parts of central and eastern India for approximately 112 years.
 
 
 
• **Pushyamitra Shunga:**
 
 
• Pushyamitra was a Brahmin by birth and served as the commander-in-chief under the Maurya ruler Brihadratha.
 
• He is known for his military campaigns and efforts to expand his kingdom.
 
• Pushyamitra is often credited with reviving the Vedic religion and promoting the Brahmanical culture.
 
• His reign saw the construction of many Hindu temples and the promotion of Sanskrit literature.
 
 
 
• **Maurya Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Maurya Dynasty was a powerful ancient Indian dynasty founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE.
 
• It is known for its significant contributions to art, culture, and politics in ancient India.
 
• The most notable ruler of the Maurya Dynasty was Ashoka, who played a crucial role in spreading Buddhism.
 
• The decline of the Maurya Empire began after Ashoka's death, eventually leading to its fall and the rise of the Shunga Dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Brahmanism:**
 
 
• Brahmanism refers to the religious and social practices of the ancient Brahmins, the priestly class in Hindu society.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of rituals, sacrifices, and the authority of the Vedas.
 
• Brahmanism played a significant role in shaping the cultural and religious landscape of ancient India.
 
• The revival of Brahmanism during the Shunga Dynasty marked a shift from the Buddhist influence that was prominent during the Maurya period.

questions.question: How many players are there on a standard ice hockey (when there is no overtime or penalties) team during a game?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A standard ice hockey team during a game, when there is no overtime or penalties, consists of **six players**.
 
• These six players include **one goaltender** and **five skaters**.
 
• The five skaters are further divided into **three forwards** and **two defensemen**.
 
• Ice hockey is played on an ice rink, which is divided into three zones: the defensive zone, the neutral zone, and the offensive zone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goaltender**

 
 
• The goaltender, also known as the goalie or netminder, is the player responsible for preventing the opposing team from scoring by blocking shots at the goal.
 
• The goaltender wears specialized equipment, including pads, a mask, and a blocker, to protect against high-speed shots.
 
 
 
• **Forwards**
 
 
• Forwards are the players primarily responsible for scoring goals and creating offensive plays.
 
• There are three types of forwards: center, left wing, and right wing.
 
• The center usually takes face-offs and plays both offensive and defensive roles, while the wingers focus on attacking and forechecking.
 
 
 
• **Defensemen**
 
 
• Defensemen are primarily responsible for preventing the opposing team from scoring and protecting their own goal.
 
• There are usually two defensemen on the ice: a left defenseman and a right defenseman.
 
• Their duties include blocking shots, disrupting opposing plays, and clearing the puck from the defensive zone.
 
 
 
• **Zones in Ice Hockey**
 
 
• The ice rink is divided into three main zones: the defensive zone, the neutral zone, and the offensive zone.
 
• The defensive zone is the area in which a team protects its own goal, the neutral zone is the central area between the two blue lines, and the offensive zone is where the team tries to score against the opposing goaltender.

questions.question: Which sport features the "Breaststroke" as a technique?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swimming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The breaststroke is one of the four main swimming strokes used in competitive swimming.
 
• It is characterized by the frog-like movements of the arms and legs, where both arms move in a half-circle simultaneously while the legs perform a frog kick.
 
• The breaststroke is considered the slowest of the competitive swimming strokes, but it is also the most energy-efficient.
 
• It is often the first stroke taught to beginners because of its simplicity and the fact that swimmers can keep their head above water for most of the time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freestyle**

 
 
• Freestyle is the fastest of the four competitive swimming strokes.
 
• It involves an alternating arm stroke and a flutter kick, where the arms move in a windmill motion while the legs kick up and down rapidly.
 
• The swimmer's face is in the water, and they turn their head to the side to breathe.
 
 
 
• **Backstroke**
 
 
• Backstroke is swum on the back, with an alternating arm stroke and a flutter kick.
 
• It is the only competitive stroke where swimmers start in the water.
 
• Like freestyle, it also involves the flutter kick, but the swimmer faces upward, which can make navigation difficult.
 
 
 
• **Butterfly**
 
 
• Butterfly is known for its unique and demanding technique, where both arms move simultaneously in a windmill motion over the water.
 
• It is accompanied by a dolphin kick, where the legs move together in a wave-like motion.
 
• This stroke is the second fastest and is considered highly technical and physically demanding.

questions.question: The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister of India, has approved a bus scheme "PM - eBus Sewa" for augmenting city bus operation by _______ e-buses on PPP model.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "PM - eBus Sewa" scheme has been approved to augment city bus operations with 10000 electric buses.
 
• This initiative aims to improve urban mobility and reduce pollution in cities by promoting the use of electric vehicles.
 
• The scheme will be implemented on a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, encouraging private sector participation in public transport.
 
• The introduction of 10000 e-buses is expected to significantly reduce carbon emissions and enhance the overall public transportation infrastructure in urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Model**

 
 
• A PPP model involves collaboration between a government agency and a private-sector company to finance, build, and operate projects such as public transportation systems, infrastructure, etc.
 
• In the context of the "PM - eBus Sewa" scheme, the PPP model will allow for shared responsibilities and risks between the government and private entities.
 
• This model is beneficial as it can leverage private sector efficiency and investment to deliver public services.
 
• It also ensures better management and maintenance of services, thus providing higher quality and reliability.
 
 
 
• **Electric Buses**
 
 
• Electric buses are powered by electricity rather than conventional fossil fuels like diesel or petrol.
 
• They are considered environmentally friendly as they produce zero emissions, helping to reduce air pollution and carbon footprint.
 
• Electric buses also tend to have lower operating and maintenance costs compared to their diesel counterparts.
 
• The adoption of electric buses is a significant step towards sustainable urban mobility and combating climate change.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Electric Buses**
 
 
• Reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and air pollutants, leading to improved air quality.
 
• Lower noise pollution, contributing to a quieter and more pleasant urban environment.
 
• Potential cost savings over the long term due to lower fuel and maintenance costs.
 
• Increased energy efficiency and the potential to use renewable energy sources for charging.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new CEO of NITI Aayog ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BVR Subrahmanyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• BVR Subrahmanyam has been appointed as the new CEO of NITI Aayog, the policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• He is a 1987 batch IAS officer of the Chhattisgarh cadre.
 
• Prior to this appointment, he served as the Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• He has extensive experience in public administration, having held various key positions in the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India)**

 
 
• NITI Aayog was established in 2015 to replace the Planning Commission, which was set up in 1950.
 
• It aims to foster cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the states on a continuous basis, recognizing that strong states make a strong nation.
 
• The primary objective of NITI Aayog is to evolve a shared vision of national development priorities, sectors, and strategies with the active involvement of states.
 
• NITI Aayog serves as a "think tank" of the government, providing both directional and policy inputs.
 
 
 
• **Chief Secretary**
 
 
• The Chief Secretary is the senior-most cadre post within the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) in a state or union territory.
 
• The Chief Secretary is the principal advisor to the Chief Minister and the Cabinet and plays a crucial role in policy formulation and implementation at the state level.
 
• The position is pivotal in maintaining the smooth functioning of the state administration and ensuring coordination among various government departments.
 
 
 
• **IAS (Indian Administrative Service)**
 
 
• The Indian Administrative Service (IAS) is one of the three All India Services of the Government of India.
 
• IAS officers hold key positions in the Union government, state governments, and public-sector undertakings.
 
• Their responsibilities include framing and implementing policies, overseeing administration, and ensuring the enforcement of laws and regulations.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Quasi-Judicial Bodies in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission is a quasi-judicial body established under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.
 
• It deals with complaints where the value of goods/services and compensation claimed is between Rs. 20 lakhs and Rs. 1 crore.
 
• The primary objective of this commission is to provide an effective and efficient platform for consumers to resolve their disputes.
 
• This body has the authority to adjudicate consumer complaints and disputes, thus ensuring consumer rights are protected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court**

 
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It is not a quasi-judicial body but a constitutional court with the power of judicial review.
 
 
 
• **Inter-State Council**
 
 
• The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body set up on the basis of provisions in Article 263 of the Constitution of India.
 
• It aims to facilitate coordination between states and the central government.
 
 
 
• **Zonal Council**
 
 
• Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
 
• They are advisory bodies aimed at promoting cooperation and coordination between states and the center.
 
 
 
• **Quasi-Judicial Bodies**
 
 
• Quasi-Judicial Bodies are institutions that have powers akin to those of the law courts but are not courts in a strict sense.
 
• They are established to adjudicate disputes, enforce regulations, and ensure compliance with laws within their specific domain.
 
• Examples include consumer forums, income tax appellate tribunals, and the Central Information Commission.

questions.question: To which of the following states does the folk dance Khoria belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Khoria dance** is a traditional folk dance that belongs to the state of Haryana in India.
 
• The dance is usually performed by women during the **harvest season** and other festive occasions.
 
• Khoria dance is characterized by its **graceful movements** and rhythmic steps, often performed in a circle.
 
• The dancers typically wear traditional **Haryanvi attire**, which includes ghagra-choli and odhni (a type of headscarf).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Haryana**:

 
 
• Haryana is a state in northern India, known for its **rich cultural heritage** and vibrant folk traditions.
 
• The state is famous for its **agricultural productivity**, being one of the leading producers of wheat and rice in the country.
 
• Haryana has a diverse range of folk dances and music, which play an integral role in the state's cultural landscape.
 
• In addition to Khoria, other popular folk dances of Haryana include **Ghoomar, Loor, and Phag dance**.
 
 
 
• **Folk Dance**:
 
 
• Folk dances are traditional dances that originate among the common people of a region.
 
• These dances are typically passed down through generations and are often performed during local festivals, celebrations, and social gatherings.
 
• Folk dances reflect the **cultural and social life** of the people, often telling stories of their daily lives, seasons, and historical events.
 
• Costumes, music, and instruments used in folk dances are usually unique to the region and are an important aspect of the performance.
 
 
 
• **Harvest Season**:
 
 
• The harvest season is a crucial period in the agricultural calendar when crops are gathered from the fields.
 
• This season is often marked by various **celebrations and festivities** as it signifies abundance and prosperity for the farming community.
 
• In India, different regions celebrate the harvest season with unique festivals such as **Pongal, Baisakhi, Makar Sankranti, and Onam**.
 
• Folk dances and songs are an integral part of these celebrations, expressing joy and gratitude for a bountiful harvest.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Attire**:
 
 
• Traditional attire refers to the clothing that is typical of a particular region, culture, or community.
 
• In Haryana, traditional attire for women includes the **ghagra-choli** (a long skirt and blouse) and the **odhni** (a headscarf or veil).
 
• Men typically wear the **dhoti-kurta** or **kurta-pajama** along with a turban.
 
• These traditional garments are often adorned with intricate embroidery, mirror work, and vibrant colors, reflecting the cultural richness of the region.

questions.question: According to the 2011 Census of India, the proportion of ________ population has declined by 0.2 PP (percentage point).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census of India, the Sikh population has shown a decline of 0.2 percentage points in its proportion to the total population of the country.
 
• The Sikh community forms a significant part of the population in the state of Punjab, where they are the majority.
 
• Despite the decline in percentage, the absolute number of Sikhs has increased due to the overall population growth of India.
 
• Sikhism is a monotheistic religion that originated in the Punjab region of India during the 15th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India:**

 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every ten years and is one of the most comprehensive demographic surveys in the world.
 
• It collects data on various parameters including population size, composition, literacy, and housing.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country.
 
• This data is crucial for planning and policy-making at both national and state levels.
 
 
 
• **Population Proportion:**
 
 
• Population proportion refers to the percentage of a specific group within the total population.
 
• This metric helps in understanding the demographic composition and changes over time.
 
• A decline in proportion can occur even if the absolute number of individuals in that group increases, due to faster growth rates in other groups.
 
 
 
• **Sikh Community:**
 
 
• Sikhs are followers of Sikhism, a religion founded by Guru Nanak in the 15th century.
 
• The community is known for its distinct cultural and religious practices, including the wearing of turbans and the Five Ks (Kesh, Kara, Kanga, Kachera, and Kirpan).
 
• They have a significant presence in India, especially in the state of Punjab.

questions.question: The Bardoli Satyagraha took place in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bardoli Satyagraha took place in the year **1928** under the leadership of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
 
• It was a major peasant movement in the Bardoli taluka of Gujarat.
 
• The movement was initiated as a response to the increase in land revenue assessment by the British government.
 
• Due to the success of the movement, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel earned the title of "Sardar" or leader.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bardoli Satyagraha:**

 
 
• The Bardoli Satyagraha was a pivotal event in the Indian independence movement, particularly focusing on agrarian issues.
 
• The British government increased the land revenue by 22% in the Bardoli taluka, which was met with strong opposition from the peasants.
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel led the movement with the help of local leaders and the peasants decided to refuse payment of the increased taxes.
 
• The satyagraha involved non-cooperation and civil disobedience as tools to oppose the unjust tax hike.
 
• The movement gained widespread support and eventually, the British government had to roll back the increased tax assessment, marking it as a significant victory for the peasants.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:**
 
 
• Vallabhbhai Patel was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a prominent figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He played a crucial role in the integration of princely states into the Indian Union post-independence, earning him the title "Iron Man of India".
 
• Patel's leadership in the Bardoli Satyagraha showcased his organizational skills and commitment to nonviolent resistance.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Bardoli Satyagraha:**
 
 
• The success of the Bardoli Satyagraha boosted the morale of the Indian independence movement and demonstrated the effectiveness of nonviolent resistance.
 
• It highlighted the plight of Indian peasants under colonial rule and brought agrarian issues to the forefront of the national struggle for independence.
 
• The movement also solidified Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's position as a key leader in the Indian National Congress and the independence movement.

questions.question: ________ unveiled the Logo, Theme and Website of India's G20 Presidency in Virtual mode. (November 2022)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi unveiled the Logo, Theme, and Website of India's G20 Presidency in a virtual mode in November 2022.
 
• The G20 is an international forum for the governments and central bank governors from 19 countries and the European Union (EU).
 
• India's G20 Presidency marks a significant moment in its diplomatic calendar and showcases India's leadership on the global stage.
 
• Under India's Presidency, various key issues such as economic growth, financial stability, climate change, and sustainable development will be discussed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **G20 (Group of Twenty)**

 
 
• The G20 is an international forum for the governments and central bank governors from 19 countries and the European Union (EU).
 
• Founded in 1999, the G20 aims to discuss policy pertaining to the promotion of international financial stability.
 
• The G20 has expanded its agenda since 2008 to include issues such as climate change mitigation, global health, and sustainable development.
 
• The members of the G20 represent around 85% of the global GDP, over 75% of global trade, and about two-thirds of the world's population.
 
 
 
• **India's G20 Presidency**
 
 
• India assumed the G20 Presidency in December 2022, marking a significant milestone in its diplomatic engagements.
 
• During its presidency, India is expected to host various events and meetings culminating in the G20 Leaders' Summit.
 
• The theme for India's G20 Presidency is "One Earth, One Family, One Future," highlighting the interconnectedness of the world in addressing global challenges.
 
• Key priorities for India include inclusive growth, green development, digital transformation, and reform of multilateral institutions.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Mode Events**
 
 
• Virtual mode events have become increasingly common due to the COVID-19 pandemic, allowing for international diplomacy to continue despite travel restrictions.
 
• Virtual events use digital platforms to facilitate real-time communication and collaboration among participants across the globe.
 
• They offer flexibility, reduced costs, and the ability to engage a broader audience.
 
• India has effectively utilized virtual platforms for various international engagements, including the unveiling of the G20 Logo, Theme, and Website.

questions.question: Which of the following sports is played by Siddharth Suchde?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Squash**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Siddharth Suchde is a professional squash player from India who has represented the country at various international events.
 
• He has achieved a career-high world ranking of 39 in squash.
 
• Suchde has been a significant figure in promoting and popularizing the sport of squash in India.
 
• He has won several national and international titles, contributing to his recognition as one of India's top squash players.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Squash**

 
 
• Squash is a racket sport played by two (singles) or four players (doubles) in a four-walled court with a small, hollow rubber ball.
 
• The players take turns hitting the ball against the front wall, trying to make it difficult for the opponent to play a valid return.
 
• Squash is known for its high speed, agility, and strategic play, requiring a combination of physical fitness, precision, and tactical thinking.
 
• Major squash tournaments include the British Open, the U.S. Open, and the World Squash Championships.
 
 
 
• **Other Sports Mentioned**
 
 
• **Football:** A team sport where two teams of eleven players each try to score by getting a ball into the opposing team's goal using any part of their body except their hands and arms.
 
• **Badminton:** A racket sport played using rackets to hit a shuttlecock across a net. It can be played in singles or doubles format.
 
• **Tennis:** A racket sport that can be played individually against a single opponent (singles) or between two teams of two players each (doubles). Players use a stringed racket to hit a ball over a net into the opponent's court.
